5.1.4 Anti-DiabeticType II diabetes and obesity are considered two major challenges facing global public health. Tripterygium wilfordii polyglycoside can act as a proteasome inhibitor, helping to reduce insulin resistance and enhance β-cell function. Tripterygium wilfordii polyglycoside can also combat Type II diabetes by inhibiting NF-κB activation in adipose tissue, reducing oxidative stress, increasing glucose uptake via the PI3K/Akt pathway, and improving mitochondrial function.  
5.1.5 AntiviralTriptolide also possesses antiviral properties. Triptolide exhibits inhibitory effects on a viral transactivator factor Tat, thereby suppressing HIV transcription and replication. Triptolide also has beneficial effects on Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS). Additionally, triptolide can inhibit dengue virus replication by inducing IFN-α expression and activating downstream JAK-STAT signaling.  
**5.2 The Effects and Mechanisms of Tripterygium wilfordii Polysaccharides on Autoimmune Diseases**
5.2.1 Rheumatoid Arthritis
B cell infiltration in mice, exerting immunosuppressive effects, and alleviating symptoms such as joint redness and swelling. Furthermore, triptolide polymer micelles based on reactive oxygen-sensitive polymers can enhance the delivery efficiency of triptolide. These micelles inhibit macrophage polarization toward the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype via the NF-κB and Notch1 pathways, thereby improving arthritis symptoms in mice.
5.2.3 Autoimmune HepatitisAutoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an inflammatory chronic liver disease. Triptolide can alleviate liver injury and hepatic inflammatory cell infiltration in ConA-induced autoimmune hepatitis model mice when administered via gavage. Triptolide can improve liver inflammation and fibrosis in mice with acute liver injury and chronic autoimmune hepatitis through the PI3K/AKT pathway. Through the IL-6/STAT3 signaling pathway, triptolide can inhibit Th17 cell responses in mice, thereby reducing IL-17 secretion in the liver, significantly alleviating ConA-induced liver injury, and it can also inhibit hepatocyte apoptosis, thus exerting an immunoregulatory effect in mouse models of autoimmune hepatitis. Plasma metabolomics studies in autoimmune hepatitis model mice have shown that triptolide can restore the homeostasis of plasma bile acid metabolism and fatty acid metabolism, upregulate hepatic hyodeoxycholic acid levels, activate autophagy mediated by the liver pregnane X receptor (PXR) and transcription factor EB (TFEB), and reduce hepatic inflammatory cell infiltration and liver injury in mice with autoimmune hepatitis.
